title: Metric stencil for fastpath inference - notes
content:
Context and goal:
We need a compact, copyable "metric stencil" focused on the fastpath token-serving surface (first-token and steady-state short sequences). Target audience: SREs, serving-runtime eng, and dashboard curators.

Why a stencil?
- Many dashboards currently mix long-tail model workloads with the fastpath view, hiding actionable latency/cold-cache signals.
- Fastpath has different SLOs and remediation (kv warming, prefix cache, kernel selection) so the signal set should be small, high-fidelity, and cheap to query.

High level signal groups (candidate minimal set):
1) Request-level timing (primary):
   - req.received_ts (event) — trace anchor
   - fastpath.time_to_first_token_ms — histogram (p50/p95/p99)
   - fastpath.time_to_last_token_ms — histogram (for short sequences)
   - fastpath.kv_lookup_ms — histogram (if applicable)
   - fastpath.queue_wait_ms — histogram (time spent in scheduler queue)
   Rationale: These let operators separate scheduling, KV, kernel and model execution time.

2) Cache/kv health:
   - kv.cache_hit.boolean (tag) or kv.cache_hit_rate (%) per model-route
   - kv.warmth_index — small integer (0/1/2) representing cold/warming/hot for a tenant or model
   - kv.eviction_count per host per minute
   Rationale: Fastpath latency sensitivity is dominated by cache warmth. Keep it cheap: one rollup per tenant/model.

3) Model variant routing and fallback counts:
   - routing.variant_used (enum)
   - routing.fallback_count (counter)
   Rationale: Alerts for unexpected fallback spikes.

4) Error and degradation signals:
   - fastpath.error_rate (per-route) — counter for 4xx/5xx split
   - fastpath.hallucination_regressions (for quality-linked alerts) — optional link to eval job IDs

5) Load and batching context:
   - batch.size.histogram (continuous)
   - concurrency.active_workers (gauge) by pool

Metric definition notes (concrete):
- All timing metrics: milliseconds, histograms with exponential buckets, store p50/p90/p95/p99 aggregations.
- Use tags: model_name, model_variant, route, tenant_id (or tenant_bucket), region, pool_id. Keep tag cardinality low; prefer tenant_bucket over raw tenant ID for dashboards.
- Metric names should start with subsystem, e.g., fastpath.* for this stencil.

Tracing anchors and span conventions:
- Root span: request:request_id. Add attributes: route, model_name, tenant_bucket, pool_id.
- Anchor spans to correlate:
   - span.kv_lookup (duration) with attribute kv_hit=true/false and kv_ttl when available.
   - span.scheduler_queue (duration) with queue_depth metric annotation.
   - span.kernel_exec (duration) with hardware tags (gpu_model, device_id) and quantization tag (int8/float16).
- Sampling: aggressive adaptive sampling for fastpath failures and p99 slow traces; for normal traffic sample 0.1% but always keep traces when kv_hit=false or queue_wait_ms > X ms (X = alert threshold).

Dashboard tiling recommendations (compact fastpath panel set):
- Tile 1: Fastpath latency heatmap (p95) by tenant_bucket vs region for last 6h. Purpose: see tenant outliers.
- Tile 2: Time series: time_to_first_token_p95 with inline kv_hit_rate (dual axis). Purpose: correlate cache with latency.
- Tile 3: Micro-sparkline: batch.size_p50/p95 per pool (thin). Purpose: detect sudden batch size changes affecting latency.
- Tile 4: Trace sample link: quick link to last 20 p99 traces with annotated kv_hit boolean.
- Tile 5: Alert summary: counts of fallback spikes, kv.eviction bursts, and queue over-threshold events.

Query cost and rollup guidance:
- Use 1m rollups for operational panels, 5m for long-term.
- For tenant-level dashboards, prefer pre-aggregated rollups (per-tenant_bucket per-minute) to avoid high-cardinality queries.
- Store histograms as typed histograms; avoid exploding series by heavy tag expansion in dashboards.

Experiment ideas (short-lived pilots):
- Warmth synthetic probe: a lightweight probe that runs a canonical prefix for high-value tenants every X minutes and records kv.warmth_index. Validate correlation with first-token latency.
- Adaptive trace-trigger: sample 100% of single-tenant requests that exceed time_to_first_token_p95 by +20% for 15 minutes after a burst, to gather context.

Operational runbook snippets:
- On fastpath p95 spike: check kv_hit_rate -> if low, trigger kv-prefetch job and inspect eviction_count; if kv_hit stable, check queue_wait_ms and pool capacity.
- On fallback increase: check routing.variant_used histogram; inspect recent deploys/rollouts (linked_artifacts).

Open questions / decisions to make:
- tenant_bucket sizing: static (top-100 + remainder) vs dynamic bucketing. Tradeoffs noted in JIRA: OBS-4121.
- Exact trace sampling thresholds (current heuristic suggested above). Need cost simulation.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- [Rohan] Create example Grafana panel JSONs for the 5 tiles (template with tenant_bucket variable) — due 2025-11-18.
- [Aisha] Prototype warmth synthetic probe (kitchen-run) and open perf PR — due 2025-11-20.
- [Nina] Run query-cost simulation for 1m vs 5m rollups on sample traffic — due 2025-11-17.

Appendix: quick metric naming cheat-sheet
- fastpath.time_to_first_token_ms (hist)
- fastpath.time_to_last_token_ms (hist)
- fastpath.kv_lookup_ms (hist)
- fastpath.queue_wait_ms (hist)
- kv.cache_hit_rate (gauge/rollup)
- kv.warmth_index (gauge)
- routing.variant_used (label/hist)
- batch.size (hist)

Notes to self: keep this stencil intentionally small. If a use-case requires more detailed telemetry, create a use-case-specific doc (e.g., embeddings fastpath vs chat fastpath).

References and links: see linked_artifacts header. Also: slack:#obs-ops thread "fastpath-warmth-impl" and confluence page OBS-METRICS-2025 for background.
